title: Annotatio IV §.XVII open: Ages XII–XIII+ — Waldenses first Reformers against Innocent’s Transubstantiation
pass_a_gloss: §. XVII. But just as in the XIIth AGE, so no less in the XIIIth and following, the most famous Waldenses constantly and strongly disapproved both the papal life and the papal doctrine — especially concerning Transubstantiation established by the authority of Innocent III — so that on this account they not only hold a chief place among the witnesses of Christian truth but also deserve to be called the first Reformers of the Roman Church.
pass_b_english: §.XVII: in Ages XII and XIII and after, the famous Waldenses steadily rejected papal life and doctrine — above all Transubstantiation fixed by Innocent III.
For that they hold a chief place among Christian-truth witnesses and deserve to be called the Roman Church’s first Reformers.
source_text: §. XVII. Sicuti verò SECULO XII, ita non minus XIII, & seqq. famosissimi Waldenses tàm vitàm, quàm doctrinam papalem, maximè de Transsubstantiatione, Innocentii III. auctoritate stabilitam, constanter & fortiter improbarunt, ut hoc nomine non præcipuum duntaxat locum inter veritatis Christianæ testes teneant, sed & primi Ecclesiæ Romanæ Reformatores dici mereantur.
